options.description: Every letter waits for your answers to the three questions. There is no skip path and no neutral opening. A letter the employer forbids is not drafted, so no questions are asked for it. Recommended: Your words say 'always', so the first option is the closest to them. The skip path is a new behaviour you did not mention, so it should only be added if you ask for it.
options.label: Always ask, no skip (Recommended)

options.description: You can skip the questions. The letter then gets a neutral opening with the gap noted, and no enthusiasm is invented. Forbidden-letter cases still ask nothing.
options.label: Allow an explicit skip

payload.question:
You said the cover letter workflow should always clarify why a company, your other motivations and what you want to put forward. Should it ever go ahead without your answers, either because you choose to skip the questions or because the employer forbids a letter?

You said on 2026-11-16: "cover letter workflow should always clarify with questions why a given company, and other motivational aspects, and what the user would like to put forward in the cover letter."
